The major investment firm has taken interest in Bitcoin, and they're trying to see if they can see the next step in the money's evolution. On safety. And they believe Bitcoin is similar to salt and that Bitcoin will truly be digital gold,. As you can see from this chart where Bitcoin is surpassing the gold price. Welcome aboard,. Merrill Lynch. We've also got great news from Fortune magazine. LedgerX just gave us another. Way to bet against Bitcoin. Isn't that great? Actually, you can bet for Bitcoin as well. They're opening futures and options trading markets via Ledger X. These are also approved by the CFTC, the Commodities Future Trading Commission, the first approved Bitcoin derivatives. Interesting stuff. We're also joined by Jimmy Song. How's it going, Jimmy? It's going great. I want to point out that the CFTC, one of the reasons that they gave for the. Winklevoss ETF not being approved was that they didn't have any other regulatory agencies that. Sort of already approved it. This may give a path for another ETF to get into the mainstream. So. So that's that's good news as well. But yeah, it's been going great. I've been analyzing some of the Bitcoin ABC code, looking at Bitcoin Cash and things like. That. One one, a couple of notes. They changed the replay protection scheme so that it's not one way any longer. It used to be that if you made a transaction on Bitcoin Cash, it wasn't replayable in Bitcoin,. But not the other way around. It's two-way because they merged in a something I think it was yesterday night. That made it so that it's based on sig hash fork ID a little bit technical but. Basically it makes it so that transactions on one are not replayable. On the other in both directions so great news for a lot of exchanges and wallets. And things like that because you don't have to worry about this stuff if. If customers are asking for funds. Another thing that I did was I posted a tweet earlier today. About just a very rough look at what Bitcoin ABC is. It's based on core 0.14.0. It has a lot of commits,. Most of which are actually like formatting C++ and things like that. But it removes replace by fee. It removes segwit. It adds the UAHF spec that Bitmain wrote about a month ago. And it's mostly two developers, F-Trader and Dead Linux. So that's something that you should keep in mind if you're thinking about doing anything with it. Jimmy, what about the block size? I've heard they're going to instantly raise it to 8 megabytes. Is that true? Yeah, so it is going to be raised to eight megabytes. The only real restriction, I think it's based on the emerging consensus sort of idea from Bitcoin Unlimited. Uh but so it can get larger than eight megabytes but there's sort of like a soft limit at eight. Megabytes at least initially uh and the forking block has to be greater than one megabyte with. All of these um with uh sig sig hash hard fork or whatever so um you know that's going to be. Interesting because i i think those are going to have to be uh manufactured manually because i i. Almost always been throughput and bandwidth. And, you know, obviously a lot of ISPs restrict sort. To upload speed significantly versus download. I imagine it might be one percent of Bitcoin. It might be half a percent. It might be five percent. And it'll go up and down constantly. So you might find a lot of blocks quickly. And depending on how their difficulty adjustment thing plays out,. It may be that you find a ton of blocks really quickly. So that's something to keep track of. If the block size limit was 10 megabytes as of 2010 or 11 when he added it, we could be looking at a 5x bigger blockchain size today in total. And then storage would become a problem because now we're pushing onto a terabyte in order to keep the history of transactions. I also think it's insane to have two people code your Bitcoin source code, and one of them has a name of DeadLinux. So that's perfect.
